notes: MTK952 is a 1U rack dual-channel wireless IEM/wideband transmitter, not a typical video/AV switching device — categorized here as "audio"/"Wireless mic" since no better-fitting category exists in the schema. Rear-panel data extracted directly from the manufacturer's official MTK952 User Manual (rev.09, dated 22 Oct 2018), page 5 "Rear Panel" diagram, which numbers and labels every connector explicitly. No bandwidth "grade" was set on any port: RJ45 (Ethernet, used only for configuration via Wisycom Manager software) has no stated link speed in the manual; AES3/XLR3 digital audio and BNC RF/antenna/master-slave ports are outside the gradeable connector categories per the schema's grading rules (SDI/HDMI/DP/USB/RJ45 speed only) so grade was correctly omitted even though AES3 and RF are technically \"digital\"/bandwidth-relevant. The optional DC power connector is a 4-pin circular connector (pinout diagram shows 1/3=GND, 2/4=+Vdc) — mapped to xlr4-dc as the closest listed connector type; Wisycom's own accessories (e.g. battery eliminators for companion receivers) commonly use 4-pin XLR for DC, supporting this mapping, but the manual itself does not explicitly say \"XLR\" for this specific plug. Two hardware variants exist: MTK952 (BNC antenna connectors) and MTK952N (N-type antenna connectors) — I used the base MTK952 (BNC) as the primary model per the requested name; note this if the N-variant is intended. Power options also vary (0W2/50mW, 2W0/2W max output) but these don't affect the I/O list. Manufacturer's own product page (wisycom.com/product/mtk952) and PDF spec sheet returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, so the manual PDF (hosted on wisycom.com/app/uploads) was used as the primary source instead, cross-verified against a WebSearch-summarized secondary manual mirror (usermanual.wiki) which matched exactly.
